title: `--checkpoint-remote` supports only the `github` provider — no self-hosted/generic git remote option

verdict.rationale: The provider-restricted, structured `provider:owner/repo` format was chosen deliberately so other backends could be supported later. The GitLab commit widened the provider list on purpose while documenting self-hosted hosts as an open, deferred question, so restricting to known providers was intentional rather than accidental.

evidence.text:
feat: structured checkpoint_remote config with fork detection

Replace the raw URL checkpoint_remote setting with a structured format:
{"provider": "github", "repo": "org/repo"}. At push time, the actual
git URL is derived from the push remote's protocol (SSH vs HTTPS) so
authentication works automatically. Fork detection compares the push
remote owner to the checkpoint repo owner and skips pushing when they
differ. Named git remotes are no longer created — pushes go directly
to the derived URL.

- the remote currently used can be using git or http auth with github, the setting url should support both for GitHub urls

- forks might need to be handled differently, makes no sense to give them a remote they most likely can't access anyhow
